notes: Matches the reference: Token methods treat only unquoted braces as structural across the dispenser, directive, import/snippet and blockTokens paths. It misses two minor spots the reference fixed: the quoted-address `HasSuffix("{")` check and the quoted `"{}"` branch in directive(). Tests are thorough and well targeted.

Fixes the issue at its root by adding unquoted-brace helper methods on Token and using them consistently in the dispenser, parser, import, snippet and blockTokens paths; it misses two minor spots the reference covers: a quoted address ending in `{` still trips the HasSuffix error, and a quoted "{}" still bypasses the newline break; its dispenser, parser and snippet tests are thorough.

It fixes the reported same-module case by returning a slice of import statements, but it still dedups on ConfigResource across modules, so a parent block for module.child.res["a"] silently drops a child block for res["b"] — the same silent-discard bug the issue describes, unlike the reference's instance-level dedup at expansion time (2 of 3 hidden tests fail). Its new unit test even encodes that drop as expected behaviour, and it adds a changelog entry with Issue "TODO".

Fixes the reported root-module case by keeping every same-module block, but parent-over-child override is still decided per ConfigResource rather than per instance. A child import of a different instance (e.g. baz["b"] when the parent imports baz["a"]) is still silently dropped, the same class of bug as the issue, and its own fixture encodes that as expected. This likely explains failing 2 of 3 hidden tests; it also ships a changelog entry with Issue "TODO".

It recursively builds the slug-applied section base and remaps the container dir on path boundaries, so section, nested-section, section-less leaf, taxonomy and term slugs all propagate correctly; it keeps a slightly redundant Section/SectionBase pair where the reference uses a single Dir field, and the integration test is thorough.

Applies section, taxonomy and term slugs to section and descendant paths through a recursive helper, plus a prefix rewrite of containerDir; it is correct and well covered by a test of nested sections, non-section subdirectories, taxonomies and terms, though keeping both Section and SectionBase and rewriting prefixes inside CreateTargetPaths is less direct than computing the final Dir up front.

Correctly rewrites the consolidated options into a single 1-VU/1-iteration shared-iterations scenario, keeping exec, env, tags and options, rejecting multiple scenarios and the vus/duration/iterations/stage flags, and reaching archive and cloud through the shared path; however, unlike the reference it does not strip shortcuts from lower layers before the merge, so a K6_ITERATIONS or K6_DURATION env var still wipes the script's scenario, and it neither rejects the execution-segment flags nor preserves an unset exec as unset.

Applies --once correctly after consolidation for the documented cases (no scenario, single scenario, multiple scenarios, shortcut-flag conflicts) and has thorough unit, run and archive tests; however, it does not drop shortcut options set in lower config layers (env, config file), which can wipe the script's scenarios before applyOnce runs, it omits the execution-segment conflicts, and it turns an unset exec into an explicit "default".

Fixes the root cause the same way as the reference: a parenthesised NumberLiteral becomes a Wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr, in both paren_duration_expr and applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr. It also extends the zero-division, zero-modulo and positive-duration parse checks so that `(0)` and `-(5s)` are still rejected at parse time. Gaps: DurationExpr.Pretty is not updated for unary plus as the reference does, and the wrapper's position range omits the surrounding parens. Tests cover round-trip, parse errors and evaluation thoroughly.

Fixes the bug the same way the reference does, by lifting a parenthesised NumberLiteral into a Wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr in both the paren and unary paths, and adds `constantDurationValue` so the parse-time checks for division/modulo by zero and non-positive durations still fire on the new AST shape (the reference loses those checks); minor gaps are that `DurationExpr.Pretty` is not updated to suppress unary plus, and `StartPos` uses the number's position rather than the opening paren, though tests are thorough across printer, parser errors and evaluation.

The sentinel-error approach matches the issue, and early returns now work anywhere, but the patch has several problems. It changes the public Executer/ExecuteWithContextAndKey signatures to `(any, error)`, keeps an AST rewrite (moveReturnLast) and the static HasReturn flag, and copies walkTemplate's body instead of wrapping the renamed walkTemplateOld. On edge cases it diverges from expected behaviour: `{{ return nil }}` becomes the 'nil is not a command' error, value returns in non-partials and inside `{{ template }}` are silently swallowed, and mid-pipeline returns are rewritten rather than rejected. It also edits an existing test expectation to fit its new behaviour, and the package suite fails.

The core panic-sentinel mechanism works, so early return now functions anywhere, but there are several problems: `{{ return nil }}` breaks ('nil is not a command'); `{{ return . | upper }}` is silently rewritten through an AST transform, which keeps the transform complexity the issue wanted removed; a valued return in non-partials is ignored rather than reported as an error; whether a partial returns a value is decided statically by `HasReturn`, so one that never reaches its return yields nil instead of its output; the patch changes the exported `Executer` and `TemplateStore` signatures, copies the `walkTemplate` body instead of wrapping `walkTemplateOld`, and edits an existing test's expected error, consistent with the 2 hidden-test failures and the failing suite.
